1	# Business Requirements Document: Credit Control
2	
3	| | |
4	|---|---|
5	| Prepared for | Finance Director |
6	| Prepared by | Business Analyst, Finance |
7	| Version | 1.0 (draft for sign-off) |
8	| Status | For review by Finance, Sales and IT |
9	
10	## 1. Purpose
11	
12	This document sets out what the business needs from a credit control capability in our ERP system. Today credit control lives in a spreadsheet and in the head of our credit controller. The board has asked that it move into the ERP, so that the same rules are applied to every customer every time, so that sales staff and customers cannot get around them, and so that our auditors can see what was decided, by whom and when.
13	
14	The document describes the business behaviour we want. It does not say how the software should be built.
15	
16	## 2. Background
17	
18	We are a wholesale distributor with about 900 trade customers on account. Customers are billed in several currencies. Orders reach us in four main ways: entered by our sales office, placed by customers through our web shop, sent to us electronically by larger customers, and raised automatically from standing monthly orders.
19	
20	Last financial year our bad debt write-offs were well above what the board considers acceptable. A review found the main causes were:
21	
22	- Customers kept being supplied after they had stopped paying, because the "stop list" was a spreadsheet that the sales office and the web shop did not check.
23	- Credit limits were set once when the account was opened and rarely looked at again.
24	- Reminder letters were sent irregularly, depending on how busy the credit controller was.
25	- We charged no interest or late fees, so slow payers had no reason to pay on time.
26	- Write-offs were posted inconsistently, and at year end the auditors had trouble matching the sales ledger to the general ledger and to the decisions behind each write-off.
27	
28	We already use the ERP for sales orders, invoicing, customer accounts, statements and the general ledger, so the credit control work should sit there too.
29	
30	## 3. Stakeholders
31	
32	| Stakeholder | Interest |
33	|---|---|
34	| Finance Director (sponsor) | Lower bad debt, consistent control, a clean audit. |
35	| Maria, Credit Controller | Runs credit control day to day: reviews, stops, reminders, charges, write-offs. |
36	| Deputy Credit Controller | Covers for Maria with the same authority. |
37	| Financial Accountant | Month-end close; the ledger must agree with customer accounts. |
38	| Sales Manager and sales reps | Need to know which of their customers are on stop or on watch; must not be able to override it. |
39	| Sales office / order entry | Must be stopped from processing orders for customers on stop. |
40	| Customers | See their own reminders, interest and fees; receive reminder letters by email. |
41	| External auditors | Need a trail of credit decisions, charges and write-offs. |
42	| IT / system administrator | Installs and configures the change on our live system. |
43	
44	## 4. Scope
45	
46	### 4.1 In scope
47	
48	1. Periodic credit reviews of customers, recording the outcome, notes and the next review date.
49	2. Putting customers "on stop" (also called "on hold" or "frozen") and taking them off stop.
50	3. A softer "watch" status for customers we are worried about but still supply.
51	4. Overdue reminder letters ("chasers", "dunning letters") in escalating stages, sent by email.
52	5. Interest and/or late fees on overdue balances, charged at month end.
53	6. Writing off bad debts.
54	7. A report of customers due a credit review and customers over their credit limit.
55	8. Sales reps seeing only their own customers' credit information.
56	9. Customers seeing their own reminders and charges in the customer portal.
57	10. Month-end agreement between the general ledger and customer accounts.
58	11. Working on both our existing live system and on any new installation.
59	12. Updating the staff guide.
60	
61	### 4.2 Out of scope
62	
63	- Credit insurance and external credit-reference agency feeds.
64	- Debt collection agencies and legal proceedings (we will continue to handle these outside the system, though we want a note of them against the customer).
65	- Changes to how customers pay us, or to cash allocation.
66	- Customer credit applications and account opening.
67	- Supplier (purchase ledger) side.
68	- Changes to price lists, discounts or sales commissions.
69	
70	## 5. Business Requirements
71	
72	### 5.1 Credit reviews
73	
74	- **BR-01** Credit control must be able to record a credit review against any customer. A review records the date, who did it, the outcome (for example: limit confirmed, limit raised, limit reduced, put on watch, put on stop), any new credit limit, free-text notes and the next review date.
75	- **BR-02** Every customer on account must have a next review date. New customers get one automatically when their account is opened, based on a standard review period set by Finance (we expect 12 months, and shorter for higher-risk customers).
76	- **BR-03** The full history of reviews for a customer must be kept and viewable. Past reviews cannot be changed or deleted.
77	- **BR-04** When a review changes the credit limit, the customer's limit must update as part of the review, so the limit and the reason for it are always recorded together.
78	
79	### 5.2 Stop and watch
80	
81	- **BR-05** Credit control must be able to put a customer on stop, with a reason, and take them off stop, with a reason. Each change records who did it and when.
82	- **BR-06** While a customer is on stop, no new orders may be accepted or released for them, by any route: the sales office, the web shop, electronic orders and standing monthly orders. Goods must not be dispatched or invoiced on existing orders taken before the stop, unless credit control releases them.
83	- **BR-07** Only the credit controller and the deputy (and the Finance Director) may put customers on or off stop, or change credit limits. Sales reps and sales office staff must not be able to.
84	- **BR-08** Credit control must be able to put a customer on "watch". A customer on watch can still be supplied, but anyone taking an order for them must be clearly warned, and credit control should be able to see orders taken for watched customers.
85	- **BR-09** A customer's credit status (normal, watch or on stop) must be clearly visible wherever staff look at that customer or take an order for them.
86	- **BR-10** Orders that would take a customer over their credit limit must be held for credit control's approval rather than accepted outright. (Today reps "just put it through".)
87	- **BR-11** Where a customer has asked for or been told about a stop, the customer should see in the web shop that their account is on hold and should contact us, rather than having orders silently fail.
88	
89	### 5.3 Reminder letters (dunning)
90	
91	- **BR-12** The system must send overdue reminder letters in escalating stages. We expect three stages to start with: a polite reminder, a firmer second letter, and a final notice warning that the account will be put on stop and charges applied. Finance must be able to set the number of stages, how many days overdue triggers each stage and the wording of each letter.
92	- **BR-13** Reminders must go by email to the customer's accounts contact. Customers with no email address must be listed so that credit control can post the letter.
93	- **BR-14** Reminders are produced in a regular run (we expect weekly) started by credit control. Before sending, credit control must be able to see who will get which letter and leave out particular customers (for example, where a payment has been promised or there is a dispute).
94	- **BR-15** A customer should only move up a stage if they are still overdue; a customer who pays must not get the next letter. A customer must not receive the same stage twice in a short time.
95	- **BR-16** Every reminder sent must be recorded against the customer: the date, the stage, what invoices it covered and the amount.
96	- **BR-17** Reminders must be in the customer's own currency and show their overdue invoices.
97	- **BR-18** Credit control should be able to mark an invoice as disputed, so that it is not chased and not charged interest until the dispute is settled.
98	
99	### 5.4 Interest and late fees
100	
101	- **BR-19** At month end the system must be able to charge interest on overdue balances, a fixed late fee, or both. Finance must be able to set the interest rate, the fee amount and how many days overdue a balance must be before it is charged.
102	- **BR-20** It must be possible to exempt individual customers from interest and/or fees (for example, key accounts or those with agreed payment plans).
103	- **BR-21** Charges must be raised in the customer's own currency and must appear on the customer's account and their next statement as separate, clearly described items.
104	- **BR-22** Before charges are posted, credit control must be able to see a list of what will be charged to whom, and confirm it. The same month must not be charged twice.
105	- **BR-23** Interest and fees must post to the general ledger to the income accounts that Finance chooses.
106	- **BR-24** Credit control must be able to waive (reverse) a charge for a customer, with a reason, and the reversal must also reach the ledger.
107	
108	### 5.5 Bad debt write-off
109	
110	- **BR-25** Credit control must be able to write off all or part of a customer's unpaid balance as a bad debt, with a reason.
111	- **BR-26** Write-offs above an amount set by Finance must be approved by the Finance Director before they take effect.
112	- **BR-27** A write-off must reduce the customer's balance and post to the bad debt account in the general ledger, including any currency difference.
113	- **BR-28** When a customer has a debt written off, the customer should be put on stop automatically, unless credit control decides otherwise.
114	- **BR-29** There must be a report of write-offs over a period, showing customer, amount, reason, who did it and who approved it.
115	
116	### 5.6 Reporting
117	
118	- **BR-30** A credit control report must list customers who are due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit (and by how much), and customers on watch or on stop. It must be filterable by sales rep and by currency, and totals must be shown in our home currency.
119	- **BR-31** The aged debt report must show each customer's credit status, credit limit and the last reminder stage sent.
120	- **BR-32** All credit control actions (reviews, stop/watch changes, limit changes, reminders, charges, waivers and write-offs) must be visible as a history per customer that the auditors can inspect.
121	
122	### 5.7 Sales reps
123	
124	- **BR-33** Sales reps must see credit information (status, limit, balance, overdue amounts, reminders) only for their own customers, not for other reps' customers.
125	- **BR-34** Reps can see but not change credit status or limits.
126	
127	### 5.8 Customer portal
128	
129	- **BR-35** Customers who log in to the portal must be able to see the reminder letters we have sent them and the interest and fees charged to their account, along with their balance.
130	- **BR-36** A customer must only ever see their own account.
131	
132	### 5.9 Month end and the ledger
133	
134	- **BR-37** At month end the total of all customer balances must agree with the trade debtors control account in the general ledger, after interest, fees, waivers and write-offs have been posted.
135	- **BR-38** If they do not agree, Finance must be able to find out why from the system.
136	
137	### 5.10 Installation and rollout
138	
139	- **BR-39** The capability must work on our existing live system, with all our existing customers, balances and history, as well as on a brand-new installation.
140	- **BR-40** On go-live every existing customer starts as "normal", with a next review date set by Finance, unless credit control loads their current status from the spreadsheet. Existing customers who are on the spreadsheet stop list today must be on stop in the system from day one.
141	- **BR-41** Nothing in the new capability should change how existing invoices, statements or postings behave for customers who are not overdue.
142	
143	### 5.11 Documentation and training
144	
145	- **BR-42** The staff guide must be updated to explain credit reviews, stop and watch, the reminder run, month-end charges, write-offs and the credit control report.
146	- **BR-43** Sales staff need a short note on what "watch" and "stop" mean for them and who to contact.
147	
148	## 6. User Stories
149	
150	1. **As Maria (credit controller)**, I want to see every Monday which customers are due a review or over their limit, so that I can work through them in order and nothing slips.
151	2. **As Maria**, I want to put a customer on stop once, and know that the sales office, the web shop, EDI orders and the standing orders are all blocked, so that I don't have to phone round.
152	3. **As the deputy credit controller**, I want the same powers and the same history as Maria, so that I can cover her holidays without asking her what she agreed with whom.
153	4. **As a sales rep**, I want to see when one of my customers is on watch or on stop, and why, so that I can talk to the customer before they place an order.
154	5. **As Maria**, I want the weekly reminder run to email the right letter at the right stage to each overdue customer, after I've had a chance to take out the ones I'm already talking to.
155	6. **As the Financial Accountant**, I want month-end interest and fees to post themselves to the ledger, so that the debtors control account agrees with the customer balances without manual journals.
156	7. **As the Finance Director**, I want to approve large write-offs before they go through, so that I know what bad debt we are taking.
157	8. **As a customer**, I want to see in the portal the reminders and charges on my account, so that I understand what I owe and why.
158	9. **As the external auditor**, I want to see for any customer who changed their credit limit or status, when and why, so that I can test the credit control process.
159	
160	## 7. Acceptance Criteria (business terms)
161	
162	- **AC-01** Maria records a review on a customer, raising their limit and setting next review in six months. The new limit applies straight away, and the review, with her notes, appears in the customer's history. The customer drops off the "due for review" list and reappears when the next date comes round.
163	- **AC-02** A customer is put on stop. An order for them cannot be completed in the sales office, through the web shop, electronically or from their standing order. When they are taken off stop, orders go through again. Both changes appear in their history with reasons.
164	- **AC-03** A sales rep tries to take a customer off stop or raise a limit and cannot.
165	- **AC-04** A customer on watch places an order: it is accepted, the person taking it sees a warning, and the order shows on credit control's list.
166	- **AC-05** An order that would take a customer over their limit is held and only released when credit control approves it.
167	- **AC-06** In the reminder run, a customer 35 days overdue gets the first letter by email; the next run, if still unpaid and past the second threshold, they get the second letter; if they pay in between, they get nothing. A customer marked disputed gets no letter. Every letter sent shows on the customer's account history and in their portal.
168	- **AC-07** At month end, an overdue customer is charged interest at the set rate and the set late fee in their own currency; an exempt customer is not charged; running the charges again for the same month charges nobody twice. The charges appear on the customer's statement and in the portal.
169	- **AC-08** After month-end charges, waivers and write-offs, the total of customer balances equals the debtors control account in the general ledger.
170	- **AC-09** A write-off below the approval amount reduces the customer's balance and appears in the bad debt account; one above it does nothing until the Finance Director approves it. The customer is put on stop.
171	- **AC-10** Rep A sees credit details for her customers and none for Rep B's customers. Customer X in the portal sees only Customer X's reminders and charges.
172	- **AC-11** After go-live on the live system, all existing customers, balances and history are intact, every customer has a next review date, and everyone on the old spreadsheet stop list is on stop.
173	- **AC-12** The updated staff guide covers every item in section 4.1 and has been read and agreed by Maria and the Sales Manager.
174	
175	## 8. Assumptions
176	
177	- Customers' accounts contact email addresses are mostly up to date; credit control will clean up the rest before go-live.
178	- Each customer already has a single sales rep assigned.
179	- Our terms and conditions allow us to charge interest and late fees; Legal will confirm the wording for letters.
180	- Credit control will provide the current stop list and credit limits from the spreadsheet for go-live.
181	
182	## 9. Open Questions
183	
184	1. Interest: a simple annual rate on overdue balances, or a statutory late-payment rate? Does it differ by currency or country?
185	2. Late fee: one flat fee per month, or a fee per overdue invoice? Should it vary by currency?
186	3. Do we charge interest on interest and fees that are themselves overdue?
187	4. Should a customer be put on stop automatically after the final reminder, or only flagged for Maria to decide?
188	5. How should over-limit orders from the web shop and standing orders be handled: held for approval, or rejected with a message to the customer?
189	6. What is the approval threshold for write-offs, and does the Financial Accountant also need to sign off?
190	7. If a written-off debt is later paid, how do we want it shown?
191	8. Should reps be told the reason for a stop, or only that the customer is on stop?
192	9. Do we need the reminder letters in languages other than English for overseas customers?
193	10. Should customers be able to see "watch" status in the portal? (Our view: no.)
194	11. Who covers credit decisions when both Maria and her deputy are away?
195	12. Do head-office/branch customer groups share one credit limit, or does each branch have its own?

5. **As Maria**, I want the weekly reminder run to email the right letter at the right stage to each overdue customer, after I've had a chance to take out the ones I'm already talking to.
6. **As the Financial Accountant**, I want month-end interest and fees to post themselves to the ledger, so that the debtors control account agrees with the customer balances without manual journals.
7. **As the Finance Director**, I want to approve large write-offs before they go through, so that I know what bad debt we are taking.
8. **As a customer**, I want to see in the portal the reminders and charges on my account, so that I understand what I owe and why.
9. **As the external auditor**, I want to see for any customer who changed their credit limit or status, when and why, so that I can test the credit control process.

## 7. Acceptance Criteria (business terms)

- **AC-01** Maria records a review on a customer, raising their limit and setting next review in six months. The new limit applies straight away, and the review, with her notes, appears in the customer's history. The customer drops off the "due for review" list and reappears when the next date comes round.
- **AC-02** A customer is put on stop. An order for them cannot be completed in the sales office, through the web shop, electronically or from their standing order. When they are taken off stop, orders go through again. Both changes appear in their history with reasons.
- **AC-03** A sales rep tries to take a customer off stop or raise a limit and cannot.
- **AC-04** A customer on watch places an order: it is accepted, the person taking it sees a warning, and the order shows on credit control's list.
- **AC-05** An order that would take a customer over their limit is held and only released when credit control approves it.
- **AC-06** In the reminder run, a customer 35 days overdue gets the first letter by email; the next run, if still unpaid and past the second threshold, they get the second letter; if they pay in between, they get nothing. A customer marked disputed gets no letter. Every letter sent shows on the customer's account history and in their portal.
- **AC-07** At month end, an overdue customer is charged interest at the set rate and the set late fee in their own currency; an exempt customer is not charged; running the charges again for the same month charges nobody twice. The charges appear on the customer's statement and in the portal.
- **AC-08** After month-end charges, waivers and write-offs, the total of customer balances equals the debtors control account in the general ledger.
- **AC-09** A write-off below the approval amount reduces the customer's balance and appears in the bad debt account; one above it does nothing until the Finance Director approves it. The customer is put on stop.
- **AC-10** Rep A sees credit details for her customers and none for Rep B's customers. Customer X in the portal sees only Customer X's reminders and charges.
- **AC-11** After go-live on the live system, all existing customers, balances and history are intact, every customer has a next review date, and everyone on the old spreadsheet stop list is on stop.
- **AC-12** The updated staff guide covers every item in section 4.1 and has been read and agreed by Maria and the Sales Manager.

## 8. Assumptions

- Customers' accounts contact email addresses are mostly up to date; credit control will clean up the rest before go-live.
- Each customer already has a single sales rep assigned.
- Our terms and conditions allow us to charge interest and late fees; Legal will confirm the wording for letters.
- Credit control will provide the current stop list and credit limits from the spreadsheet for go-live.

## 9. Open Questions

1. Interest: a simple annual rate on overdue balances, or a statutory late-payment rate? Does it differ by currency or country?
2. Late fee: one flat fee per month, or a fee per overdue invoice? Should it vary by currency?
3. Do we charge interest on interest and fees that are themselves overdue?
4. Should a customer be put on stop automatically after the final reminder, or only flagged for Maria to decide?
5. How should over-limit orders from the web shop and standing orders be handled: held for approval, or rejected with a message to the customer?
6. What is the approval threshold for write-offs, and does the Financial Accountant also need to sign off?
7. If a written-off debt is later paid, how do we want it shown?
8. Should reps be told the reason for a stop, or only that the customer is on stop?
9. Do we need the reminder letters in languages other than English for overseas customers?
10. Should customers be able to see "watch" status in the portal? (Our view: no.)
11. Who covers credit decisions when both Maria and her deputy are away?
12. Do head-office/branch customer groups share one credit limit, or does each branch have its own?

```markdown

name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>

  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }

140	  - `if $i==0` -> the first `OrderQty` input gets `autofocus`.

It groups by `stkcode`, uses `ORDER BY salesqty DESC LIMIT FrequentlyOrderedItems`, and shows QOH, demand, on-order and available per row.

161	  - `mbflag=='G'` -> warning 'Phantom assemblies cannot be sold...has not been added to the order: $NewItem'.
162	  - Any other `mbflag` -> include `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`.
163	- `if isset($_POST['AssetDisposalEntered'])`:
164	  - `AssetToDisposeOf=='NoAssetSelected'` -> warning 'No asset was selected to dispose of. No assets have been added to this customer order'.
165	  - Otherwise:
166	    - Read the asset's `nbv` (`cost - accumdepn`) and `costact`.
167	    - If the 'ASSETS' category is absent, insert it.
168	    - Stock id is `ASSET-<id>`. While it already exists in `stockmaster`, increment suffix `-j`.
169	    - Insert `stockmaster` and `locstock`.
170	    - `NBV = CurrencyTolerance(DefaultCurrency)` if `nbv==0`, otherwise `nbv`. `NewItemDue = today`.
171	    - Include `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`.
172	
173	**Add to cart (the add-items fragment)**
174	1. `if isset($_POST['DeliveryDetails'])` -> meta refresh to `DeliveryDetails.php?identifier`, footer, `exit()`.
175	2. `if isset($NewItem)` -> single item.
176	   - `mbflag=='K'` -> BOM components added as lines at component quantity times `ParentQty`.
177	   - Otherwise one line.
178	3. `if isset($NewItemArray) AND isset($_POST['SelectingOrderItems'])` -> for each item, process it only if `$NewItemQty > 0`.
179	4. Discount matrix over all lines:
180	   - `DiscCat != "" AND !in_array(DiscCat, DiscCatsDone)` -> sum quantities for that `DiscCat`.
181	   - `SELECT MAX(discountrate) FROM discountmatrix WHERE salestype=DefaultSalesType AND discountcategory=… AND quantitybreak <= QuantityOfDiscCat`.
182	   - NULL -> 0, otherwise the rate.
183	   - `DiscountMatrixRate != 0` -> set `DiscountPercent = rate` on every line of that `DiscCat`, and `GPPercent = (Price*(1-rate) - StandardCost*ExRate)/(Price*(1-rate)/100)`.
184	
185	**Line update**
186	- `if isset($_GET['Delete'])`:
187	  - `Some_Already_Delivered(Delete)==0` -> `remove_from_cart(Delete,'Yes',identifier)`.
188	  - Otherwise `Quantity = QuantityAlreadyDelivered`, which preserves the delivered quantity.
189	- Then for each line, in order:
190	  1. `!isset(ItemDue_*)` -> default due date. Otherwise convert it.
191	  2. If `Quantity_*` is set and `ABS(OrderLine->Price - Price_*) > CurrencyTolerance(DefaultCurrency)`, a new price was entered.
192	     - `Discount_*` numeric and `Discount<100` -> `GPPercent=(Price*(1-Discount/100)-StandardCost*ExRate)/(Price*(1-Discount/100)/100)`.
193	     - `Discount_*` numeric and `Discount>=100` -> `GPPercent=0`.
194	     - Discount not numeric -> `GPPercent=(Price-StandardCost*ExRate)*100/Price`.
195	  3. If `GPPercent_*` is set and `ABS(OrderLine->GPPercent - GPPercent_*) >= CurrencyTolerance(DefaultCurrency)`, the price is recalculated: `Price=(StandardCost*ExRate)/(1-((GPPercent+Discount)/100))`. It shows the info message 'Recalculated the price from the GP % entered - the GP % was {old} the new GP % is {new}'.
196	  4. If neither changed, `Price = Price_*` and GP% is recalculated, with guards on `Price!=0`.
197	  5. `AllowOrderLineItemNarrative==1` -> use `Narrative_*`, otherwise `''`. `!isset(DiscountPercent)` -> 0.
198	  6. `!Is_Date(ItemDue_*)` -> warning and the default date.
199	  7. `Quantity<0 OR Price<0 OR DiscountPercentage>100 OR DiscountPercentage<0` -> warning 'The item could not be updated because you are attempting to set the quantity ordered to less than 0 or the price less than 0 or the discount more than 100% or less than 0%'. The line is skipped.
200	  8. `Some_Already_Delivered(line)!=0 AND LineItems[line]->Price != Price` -> warning 'The item you attempting to modify the price for has already had some quantity invoiced at the old price the items unit price cannot be modified retrospectively'. Skipped.
201	  9. `Some_Already_Delivered(line)!=0 AND DiscountPercent != DiscountPercentage/100` -> warning 'The item you attempting to modify has had some quantity invoiced at the old discount percent the items discount cannot be modified retrospectively'. Skipped.
202	  10. `QtyInv > Quantity` -> warning 'You are attempting to make the quantity ordered a quantity less than has already been invoiced...The quantity delivered and invoiced cannot be modified retrospectively'. Skipped.
203	  11. A change is detected when any of these differ: `Quantity`, `Price`, `ABS(DiscountPercent-DiscountPercentage/100)>CurrencyTolerance`, `Narrative`, `ItemDue`, `POLine`.
204	  12. `CheckCreditLimits>0 AND AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit==false` -> `DifferenceInOrderValue=(Quantity*Price*(1-DiscountPercentage/100))-(old Quantity*old Price*(1-old DiscountPercent))`, subtracted from `CreditAvailable`.
205	      - `CheckCreditLimits==1 AND CreditAvailable<=0` -> warning 'The customer account will breach their credit limit', `AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit=true`.
206	      - `CheckCreditLimits==2 AND CreditAvailable<=0` -> warning 'This change would put the customer over their credit limit and is prohibited', `WithinCreditLimit=false`, `CreditAvailable` restored, `AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit=true`.
207	  13. `WithinCreditLimit AND Quantity>0` -> `update_cart_item(LineNumber, Quantity, Price, DiscountPercentage/100, Narrative, 'Yes', ItemDue, POLine, GPPercent, identifier)`. Otherwise it is skipped.
208	- A quantity of 0 is never applied through the update. The line stays at its old quantity, so it can be removed only with Delete.
209

211	- `count(LineItems)>0` -> show the table, otherwise skip it.
212	- `DefaultPOLine==1` -> `ShowPOLine=1`.

214	- `QOHatLoc<Quantity AND (MBflag=='B' OR MBflag=='M')` -> row background `#EEAABB`.
215	- `QtyRemain!=QtyOrdered` -> show the invoiced breakdown.

221	**OrderDetails.php**
222	1. Cast `OrderNumber` to int, include the session, and run the header query over `salesorders`, `debtorsmaster` and `currencies`.
223	2. `DB_num_rows($GetOrdHdrResult) == 1` -> show the header. Otherwise there is no output and no message.
224	3. `$CustomerLogin == 1 AND $MyRow['debtorno'] != $_SESSION['CustomerID']` -> error 'Your customer login will only allow you to view your own purchase orders', footer, exit.
225	4. Comments are exploded on ' Inv '. A numeric part becomes a link to `PrintCustTrans.php?FromTransNo=…&InvOrCredit=Invoice`.
226	5. `qtyinvoiced > 0` -> `DisplayActualDeliveryDate = ConvertSQLDate(actualdispatchdate)`. Otherwise it is `ConvertSQLDate(itemdue)` in a red span.
227	6. The line loop accumulates `OrderTotal`, `OrderTotalVolume` and `OrderTotalWeight`.
228	7. Zero line rows produce no message.
229	
230	**InternalStockRequest.php**
231	- No guards.
232	- A loop over `$SearchResult`. Each row fetches `GetQuantityOnHand(stockid, Request->Location)`, `GetDemand(stockid, Request->Location)` and `GetQuantityOnOrder(stockid,'ALL')`. `Available = QOH - DemandQty + OnOrder`.
233	- `$i==0` -> autofocus on the first input.
234	- `Quantity<i>` defaults to 0.

236	**TopItems.php**
237	- `!isset($_POST['StockCat'])` -> `'All'`.
238	- The matching option is selected, or 'All'.
239	- The code for the PrintPDF and View handlers is not shown.
240	
241	## Decisions (summary of the key outcomes)
242	- Duplicate lines are rejected in `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`: `LineItems>0 AND SO_AllowSameItemMultipleTimes==0` and `strcasecmp(StockID,NewItem)==0` -> message and the item is not added.
243	- Item not found in `stockmaster` joined to `locstock` for the cart location -> warn, not added.
244	- `discontinued==1` -> error 'Obsolete Item', footer, exit. That ends the whole page for any item in a batch.
245	- Zero-cost rule: an item is accepted if `AllowSalesOfZeroCostItems==true`. If it is false, it is accepted only for mbflag B or M with `standardcost>0`, or for mbflag A, D or K. Otherwise the message says no cost is set up.
246	- `ExistingOrder != 0` -> `UpdateDB='Yes'` and `NewLineNo = MAX(orderlineno)+1` (0 if null or <0). `ExistingOrder == 0` -> `UpdateDB='No'`, `NewLineNo=-1`.
247	- Discount in `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`:
248	  - `MAX(discountrate)` over `quantitybreak < NewItemQty` (strictly less than).
249	  - The fragment above uses `<=`. A quantity equal to the break gets the discount in the fragment but not at first add.
250	  - Sell-through support rebates (`sellthroughsupport` by stock and by category) are added to `Discount`.
251	  - The rebate is converted at the currency rate when the currency differs from the company default.
252	- Credit check on add: `CheckCreditLimits>0 AND !AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit` -> `CreditAvailable -= round(Qty*Price*(1-Discount), CurrDecimalPlaces)`. The value `1` warns; the value `2` sets `WithinCreditLimit=false` and the line is not added.
253	- `GetPrice` is called as `GetPrice(NewItem, DebtorNo, Branch, NewItemQty)`.
254	
255	## Order and failure
256	- Cancel deletes `salesorderdetails` first, then `salesorders`. There is no transaction and no handler, so an error after the first delete leaves a header without lines.
257	- Asset disposal runs `INSERT stockcategory`, then `INSERT stockmaster`, then `INSERT locstock`, then the add to cart. There is no transaction. A failure after the category insert leaves the category orphaned; a failure after the stockmaster insert leaves an item with no `locstock` rows.
258	- The asset id uniqueness loop increments `$j` until `ASSET-<id>[-j]` is free.
259	- `add_to_cart` builds the in-memory line first and then runs the INSERT (when `UpdateDB='Yes'`). A DB failure leaves a cart line that is not in the DB.
260	- `update_cart_item` updates memory first and then the DB.
261	- `remove_from_cart` raises `CreditAvailable` before it unsets the line.
262	- None of the pages has a handler around `DB_query`; errors go to `DB_query`'s own error handler. The one exception is `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`, which shows a message on a DB error for the stock lookup.
263	- CSV upload has no file type, size or `fopen` error check. The loop `fgetcsv(..., 10000, ",")` runs per row.
264	- The credit check in the line update is not repeated per line once `AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit` is true.
265	- The default `identifier` is `date('U')`, so two orders opened in the same second share a session key.
266

318	## Conclusions
319	- Quick entry, the asset path, and ordinary additions all go through `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`. They share its duplicate, obsolete, zero-cost and credit checks.
320	- Only the single-item and array paths expand kits in `SelectOrderItems.php`. A kit component then goes through the include, which looks up the component's own `mbflag`.
321	- `SelectingOrderItems` accepts only quantities `> 0`, so a zero or blank quantity is dropped silently.
322	- The credit check in the line update stops at `CheckCreditLimits==2` only for the line that breaches it. Other lines in the same post still run, with `CreditAvailable` restored.
323	- `ExistingOrder==0` (new order) lines exist only in the session until `DeliveryDetails.php` saves them (behaviour not in this topic). On an existing order every add, update and delete writes to `salesorderdetails` immediately.
324	- Cancel refuses only when some line has `qtyinvoiced > 0`. It does not check order status or authorisation, and it keeps no audit record.
325	- `$CustomerLogin`: on a modify load and in `OrderDetails.php`, a customer login sees only its own `debtorno`. Both load paths enforce this. In `OrderDetails.php` the check runs after the header query and before output.
326	- The salesman restriction applies on modify load and on customer selection. `OrderDetails.php` has no salesman check.
327	- `OrderDetails.php` only reads. Its `(int)` cast makes a non-numeric number 0, which yields an empty page.
328	- Customer selection does not check that the branch belongs to the debtor, and nothing guards a repeated selection.
329	- The same CSV or POST repeated adds the lines again, unless `SO_AllowSameItemMultipleTimes==0` blocks the same stock id. For a CSV batch, the first duplicate prints a message for that item and the rest continue.

331	- A discount-category line that is deleted or changed can leave other lines at the old matrix rate until the next matrix pass.
332	- `InternalStockRequest.php` and `TopItems.php` share no records with order entry except the `StockID`, location and category tables. They are separate pages; a change to order entry does not reach them.
333	- `GetQuantityOnHand` and `GetDemand` use the cart `Location` in order entry and `Request->Location` in `InternalStockRequest.php`. `GetQuantityOnOrder` always uses 'ALL'.
334	
335	## Hazards
336	- The CSRF `FormID` is only sent as a hidden field. The customer selection logic shows no validation of it.
337	- Search keywords, codes and customer ids are interpolated into SQL. The code shows no escaping apart from the `(int)` cast in `OrderDetails.php`, so injection is possible.
338	- `$_GET['Delete']` has no format check. `$identifier` is not validated.

340	- A division by a zero `Price` in the GP% calculation of the discount matrix pass is not guarded. The update path guards `Price!=0`.
341	- Input errors for `TopItems.php` after submit are not validated.

# webERP sales order entry and item-selection pages (SelectOrderItems.php and its fragments), with OrderDetails.php, InternalStockRequest.php and TopItems.php

Part of [webERP: sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, master data, reporting, API…](weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/brief.md) (path from the export's root): its brief says how work moves through the area and what repairs a failed step.

This topic holds the sales order entry page `webERP/SelectOrderItems.php`, which is several fragments of one script. It loads or creates the session cart `$_SESSION['Items'.$identifier]`, selects the customer and branch, searches for items, adds them through quick entry, CSV upload and the frequently-ordered list, updates lines, applies discount matrix rates and cancels orders. It also holds three smaller pages: `OrderDetails.php` (a read-only order view), `InternalStockRequest.php` (an item list for internal stock requests) and `TopItems.php` (a report filter form).

It takes work from browser GET/POST requests and from `DeliveryDetails.php`, which links back to it. It hands work to the cart class (`includes/DefineCartClass.php`), `includes/SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`, `includes/GetPrice.php`, and the database tables.

## Contract

**In (SelectOrderItems.php):**
- GET: `ModifyOrderNumber`, `NewOrder`, `NewItem`, `identifier` (defaults to `date('U')`), `Delete`.
- POST:
  - Triggers: `QuickEntry`, `SelectingOrderItems`, `UploadFile`, `Recalculate`, `SelectAsset`, `AssetDisposalEntered`, `ChangeCustomer`, `SearchCust`, `JustSelectedACustomer`, `CancelOrder`, `DeliveryDetails`, `Search`, `Next`, `Previous`.
  - Customer search and selection: `CustKeywords`, `CustCode`, `CustPhone`, `SubmitCustomerSelection<j>`, `SelectedCustomer<j>`, `SelectedBranch<j>`.
  - Item search: `Keywords`, `StockCode`, `StockCat` (a category id or 'All'), `RawMaterialFlag` ('M'), `CustItemFlag` ('C'), `NextList`, `PreviousList`.

**Line update**
- `if isset($_GET['Delete'])`:
  - `Some_Already_Delivered(Delete)==0` -> `remove_from_cart(Delete,'Yes',identifier)`.

  2. If `Quantity_*` is set and `ABS(OrderLine->Price - Price_*) > CurrencyTolerance(DefaultCurrency)`, a new price was entered.
     - `Discount_*` numeric and `Discount<100` -> `GPPercent=(Price*(1-Discount/100)-StandardCost*ExRate)/(Price*(1-Discount/100)/100)`.
     - `Discount_*` numeric and `Discount>=100` -> `GPPercent=0`.
     - Discount not numeric -> `GPPercent=(Price-StandardCost*ExRate)*100/Price`.
  3. If `GPPercent_*` is set and `ABS(OrderLine->GPPercent - GPPercent_*) >= CurrencyTolerance(DefaultCurrency)`, the price is recalculated: `Price=(StandardCost*ExRate)/(1-((GPPercent+Discount)/100))`. It shows the info message 'Recalculated the price from the GP % entered - the GP % was {old} the new GP % is {new}'.
  4. If neither changed, `Price = Price_*` and GP% is recalculated, with guards on `Price!=0`.
  5. `AllowOrderLineItemNarrative==1` -> use `Narrative_*`, otherwise `''`. `!isset(DiscountPercent)` -> 0.

  8. `Some_Already_Delivered(line)!=0 AND LineItems[line]->Price != Price` -> warning 'The item you attempting to modify the price for has already had some quantity invoiced at the old price the items unit price cannot be modified retrospectively'. Skipped.
  9. `Some_Already_Delivered(line)!=0 AND DiscountPercent != DiscountPercentage/100` -> warning 'The item you attempting to modify has had some quantity invoiced at the old discount percent the items discount cannot be modified retrospectively'. Skipped.
  10. `QtyInv > Quantity` -> warning 'You are attempting to make the quantity ordered a quantity less than has already been invoiced...The quantity delivered and invoiced cannot be modified retrospectively'. Skipped.
  11. A change is detected when any of these differ: `Quantity`, `Price`, `ABS(DiscountPercent-DiscountPercentage/100)>CurrencyTolerance`, `Narrative`, `ItemDue`, `POLine`.

## Decisions (summary of the key outcomes)
- Duplicate lines are rejected in `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`: `LineItems>0 AND SO_AllowSameItemMultipleTimes==0` and `strcasecmp(StockID,NewItem)==0` -> message and the item is not added.
- Item not found in `stockmaster` joined to `locstock` for the cart location -> warn, not added.
- `discontinued==1` -> error 'Obsolete Item', footer, exit. That ends the whole page for any item in a batch.
- Zero-cost rule: an item is accepted if `AllowSalesOfZeroCostItems==true`. If it is false, it is accepted only for mbflag B or M with `standardcost>0`, or for mbflag A, D or K. Otherwise the message says no cost is set up.
- `ExistingOrder != 0` -> `UpdateDB='Yes'` and `NewLineNo = MAX(orderlineno)+1` (0 if null or <0). `ExistingOrder == 0` -> `UpdateDB='No'`, `NewLineNo=-1`.
- Discount in `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`:
  - `MAX(discountrate)` over `quantitybreak < NewItemQty` (strictly less than).
  - The fragment above uses `<=`. A quantity equal to the break gets the discount in the fragment but not at first add.
  - Sell-through support rebates (`sellthroughsupport` by stock and by category) are added to `Discount`.
  - The rebate is converted at the currency rate when the currency differs from the company default.
- Credit check on add: `CheckCreditLimits>0 AND !AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit` -> `CreditAvailable -= round(Qty*Price*(1-Discount), CurrDecimalPlaces)`. The value `1` warns; the value `2` sets `WithinCreditLimit=false` and the line is not added.
- `GetPrice` is called as `GetPrice(NewItem, DebtorNo, Branch, NewItemQty)`.

## Order and failure
- Cancel deletes `salesorderdetails` first, then `salesorders`. There is no transaction and no handler, so an error after the first delete leaves a header without lines.
- Asset disposal runs `INSERT stockcategory`, then `INSERT stockmaster`, then `INSERT locstock`, then the add to cart. There is no transaction. A failure after the category insert leaves the category orphaned; a failure after the stockmaster insert leaves an item with no `locstock` rows.
- The asset id uniqueness loop increments `$j` until `ASSET-<id>[-j]` is free.
- `add_to_cart` builds the in-memory line first and then runs the INSERT (when `UpdateDB='Yes'`). A DB failure leaves a cart line that is not in the DB.
- `update_cart_item` updates memory first and then the DB.
- `remove_from_cart` raises `CreditAvailable` before it unsets the line.
- None of the pages has a handler around `DB_query`; errors go to `DB_query`'s own error handler. The one exception is `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`, which shows a message on a DB error for the stock lookup.
- CSV upload has no file type, size or `fopen` error check. The loop `fgetcsv(..., 10000, ",")` runs per row.
- The credit check in the line update is not repeated per line once `AlreadyWarnedAboutCredit` is true.
- The default `identifier` is `date('U')`, so two orders opened in the same second share a session key.

**`webERP/includes/DefineCartClass.php`**

  3. The same with `debtorno=''`.

## Conclusions
- Quick entry, the asset path, and ordinary additions all go through `SelectOrderItems_IntoCart.php`. They share its duplicate, obsolete, zero-cost and credit checks.
- Only the single-item and array paths expand kits in `SelectOrderItems.php`. A kit component then goes through the include, which looks up the component's own `mbflag`.
- `SelectingOrderItems` accepts only quantities `> 0`, so a zero or blank quantity is dropped silently.
- The credit check in the line update stops at `CheckCreditLimits==2` only for the line that breaches it. Other lines in the same post still run, with `CreditAvailable` restored.
- `ExistingOrder==0` (new order) lines exist only in the session until `DeliveryDetails.php` saves them (behaviour not in this topic). On an existing order every add, update and delete writes to `salesorderdetails` immediately.
- Cancel refuses only when some line has `qtyinvoiced > 0`. It does not check order status or authorisation, and it keeps no audit record.
- `$CustomerLogin`: on a modify load and in `OrderDetails.php`, a customer login sees only its own `debtorno`. Both load paths enforce this. In `OrderDetails.php` the check runs after the header query and before output.
- The salesman restriction applies on modify load and on customer selection. `OrderDetails.php` has no salesman check.
- `OrderDetails.php` only reads. Its `(int)` cast makes a non-numeric number 0, which yields an empty page.
- Customer selection does not check that the branch belongs to the debtor, and nothing guards a repeated selection.
- The same CSV or POST repeated adds the lines again, unless `SO_AllowSameItemMultipleTimes==0` blocks the same stock id. For a CSV batch, the first duplicate prints a message for that item and the rest continue.
- The `<` versus `<=` difference above also means the quantity break is inclusive in the matrix re-application only.
- A discount-category line that is deleted or changed can leave other lines at the old matrix rate until the next matrix pass.
- `InternalStockRequest.php` and `TopItems.php` share no records with order entry except the `StockID`, location and category tables. They are separate pages; a change to order entry does not reach them.
- `GetQuantityOnHand` and `GetDemand` use the cart `Location` in order entry and `Request->Location` in `InternalStockRequest.php`. `GetQuantityOnOrder` always uses 'ALL'.

## Hazards
- The CSRF `FormID` is only sent as a hidden field. The customer selection logic shows no validation of it.
- Search keywords, codes and customer ids are interpolated into SQL. The code shows no escaping apart from the `(int)` cast in `OrderDetails.php`, so injection is possible.
- `$_GET['Delete']` has no format check. `$identifier` is not validated.
- Partial failure in asset disposal and cancel (above).
- A division by a zero `Price` in the GP% calculation of the discount matrix pass is not guarded. The update path guards `Price!=0`.
- Input errors for `TopItems.php` after submit are not validated.

230	  - If its `$Transaction` argument is true, it issues a ROLLBACK query.
231	  - Then it includes the footer and `exit()`s, so the page stops.
232	  - On success of an INSERT or UPDATE it sets `$_SESSION['LastInsertId']`.
233	  - If `$_SESSION['MonthsAuditTrail'] > 0`, rows were affected and `SQLToBeAudited` approves, it writes an `audittrail` row (transactiondate, userid, querystring).
234	- Every `DB_query` therefore stops the page on failure, but only calls that pass the transaction flag are rolled back:
235	  - Z_ChangeGLAccountCode passes `true` to `ChangeFieldInTable` and to the INSERT and the final DELETE.
236	  - The other Z_ utilities pass their `$ErrMsg` strings, and Z_ChangeSalesmanCode passes a halt flag. The condensations do not show whether they pass the transaction flag.
237	  - A failure inside a transaction without the flag leaves the transaction open, with autocommit still 0 and foreign-key checks possibly still off.
238	- Transaction helpers:
239	  - `DB_Txn_Begin` does `SET autocommit=0` and `START TRANSACTION`.
240	  - `DB_Txn_Commit` does `COMMIT` and `SET autocommit=1`.
241	  - `DB_IgnoreForeignKeys` and `DB_ReinstateForeignKeys` set `FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS` to 0 and 1.
242	- Z_ChangeGLAccountCode commits before it deletes the old `chartmaster` row. If that DELETE fails, both codes exist.
243	- Z_ChangeSalesmanCode calls `DB_Txn_Commit()` and then `DB_ReinstateForeignKeys()`. Foreign-key checks stay off until after the commit.
244	- Z_ChangeSupplierCode does not turn foreign-key checks off.
245	- `ChangeFieldInTable` (includes/MiscFunctions.php) runs `UPDATE <table> SET <field>='<new>' WHERE <field>='<old>'` with `DB_query($SQL,$ErrMsg,'',true)`, so a failure rolls back.
246	- Customers.php insert:
247	  - `GetNextTransNo(500)` runs `SELECT typeno FROM systypes ... FOR UPDATE`, then `UPDATE systypes SET typeno = typeno + 1`, then a SELECT of `typeno`, and returns that value.
248	  - The increment is committed before the customer INSERT. If validation passed but the INSERT fails, the number is consumed.
249	  - Customers.php opens no transaction around this.
250	- Customers.php delete: three separate DELETEs with no transaction.
251	- AddCustomerContacts.php, BankAccounts.php and AddCustomerNotes.php check validation before running any query.
252	- CustomerBranches.php geocodes before writing and uses `usleep(1000000)` between requests.
253	
254	## Decisions
255	- Customers.php chooses between update and insert on `isset($_POST['New'])`.
256	- Customers.php excludes `currcode` from the UPDATE when `debtortrans` count > 0.
257	- BankAccounts.php excludes `currcode` from the UPDATE when `banktrans` rows exist.
258	- BankAccounts.php refuses insert on a duplicate AccountCode only when `!isset($SelectedBankAccount)`.
259	- Customers.php refuses delete on `debtortrans`, `salesorders` and `salesanalysis`, but only warns on `www_users` and `contracts`.
260	- Z_ChangeBranchCode.php, Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php and Z_ChangeSalesmanCode.php exit on validation failure before any transaction starts.
261	- Z_ChangeGLAccountCode.php does not exit: it sets InputError and skips the work.
262	- Z_ChangeSupplierCode.php returns on validation failure.
263	- AddCustomerNotes.php and AddCustomerTypeNotes.php treat a `Priority` of any integer, including negative, as valid.
264	- All three note and contact pages compare the delete flag on `isset($_GET['delete'])`.
265	
266	## Connections
267	- `includes/ConnectDB_mysqli.php`:
268	  - It supplies `DB_query`, `DB_num_rows`, `DB_fetch_*`, `DB_data_seek`, `DB_error_no`, and `DB_Txn_Begin`, `DB_Txn_Commit`, `DB_Txn_Rollback`, `DB_IgnoreForeignKeys` and `DB_ReinstateForeignKeys`.
269	  - It also supplies the audit-trail write on INSERT and UPDATE.
270	  - Its `DB_Txn_Rollback` is never called by these pages and does not check whether a transaction is active.
271	- `includes/SQL_CommonFunctions.php`: `GetNextTransNo(500)` returns the next customer number from `systypes`. This is used by Customers.php when `AutoDebtorNo==1`.
272	- `includes/MiscFunctions.php`: `ChangeFieldInTable`, called from Z_ChangeGLAccountCode.php.
273	- `includes/DateFunctions.php`:
274	  - `FormatDateForSQL` returns the value unchanged if it is already in SQL format. Otherwise it splits on `/`, `-`, `.` or by length (6 or 8 digits) and uses `$_SESSION['DefaultDateFormat']`.
275	  - `ConvertSQLDate` and `Is_Date` live in the same file, but their bodies were not read in this topic (behaviour not in this topic).
276	- `CustomerBranches.php` (the redirect target and a sibling topic):
277	  - It requires `DebtorNo` and exits with a warning otherwise.
278	  - On insert or update of a branch it rejects an illegal or space-containing `BranchCode`, an empty one, `FwdDate` that is not numeric or above 30, and `EstDeliveryDays` that is not numeric or above 60.
279	  - It geocodes through OpenStreetMap Nominatim when `$_SESSION['geocode_integration']==1`.
280	  - Branch delete is refused for `debtortrans`, `salesanalysis`, `salesorders`, `www_users` or `contracts` rows, or when it is the customer's only branch.
281	  - Customers.php sends the user to it with `DebtorNo`, and it takes the new customer's code.
282	- `AddCustomerContacts.php` is the redirect target of Customers.php `AddContact`. Customers.php passes `DebtorNo`.
283	- Callers of these pages, found by a grep on the page names and not opened:
284	  - AddCustomerContacts.php is named in `Customers.php` and `SelectCustomer.php`.
285	  - AddCustomerNotes.php is named in `SelectCustomer.php` and `Customers.php`.
286	  - SupplierContacts.php is named in `SelectSupplier.php` and `Suppliers.php`.
287	  - BankAccounts.php is named in `BankReconciliation.php`, `CustomerReceipt.php`, `DailyBankTransactions.php`, `ImportBankTrans.php`, `Payments.php`, `RegularPaymentsSetup.php`, `SuppPaymentRun.php` and `sql/updates/5.php`.
288	  - The match list also holds hits from the grep's alternation (`Z_Change…` etc.).
289	- Shared tables:
290	  - Customer side: `debtorsmaster`, `custbranch`, `custcontacts`, `custnotes`, `debtortypenotes`, `debtortype`, `debtortrans`, `salesorders`, `salesanalysis`, `contracts`, `www_users`.
291	  - Setup and lookup tables: `salestypes`, `paymentterms`, `holdreasons`, `currencies`, `companies`, `systypes`.
292	  - Bank and ledger tables: `bankaccounts`, `banktrans`, `chartmaster`, `accountgroups`.
293	  - Supplier tables: `suppliers`, `suppliercontacts`.
294	
295	## Conclusions
296	- Customers.php refuses delete when `debtortrans`, `salesorders` or `salesanalysis` rows exist. A customer with only `www_users` or `contracts` rows still triggers the warning, but `CancelDelete` stays 0. The branches, contacts and master row are therefore deleted anyway, leaving users and contracts that point at a missing customer.
297	- Customer delete removes `custbranch` and `custcontacts` rows without any check on them, so all branches go with the customer.
298	- Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php does not call `ContainsIllegalCharacters` on the new code. Customers.php blocks `. - ' & + "` and spaces when it creates a code, and this utility lets them through.
299	- Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php updates `custcontacts`, `custnotes` and `custitem`, which Z_ChangeBranchCode.php does not touch (that one covers branch-keyed tables only).
300	- Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php does not update `debtortypenotes`, which is keyed by type and not by customer.
301	- Z_ChangeSalesmanCode.php does not check `New != Old`. When the codes are equal, the new-code existence check finds the old row and exits.
302	- Z_ChangeSupplierCode.php's `checkNewCode` allows an empty code, because `str_replace(' ','',"") == ""`. An empty NewSupplierNo would then pass; only the existence check of an empty supplierid would stop it.
303	- Z_ChangeGLAccountCode.php is a rename of 41 table/field pairs, more than the "34" its own text states. It updates `bankaccounts` and `gltrans` and similar, while `chartdetails` and others are included, so period balances follow.
304	- Re-submitting the same Z_ rename a second time is refused at the "old code does not exist" check, because the old row has been deleted.
305	- Submitting the contact, note or bank-account form a second time with no `Id` or `SelectedBankAccount` creates a duplicate contact or note. For `bankaccounts` the second insert is refused as an existing AccountCode.
306	- Customers.php rechecks existence before insert but has no lock between the check and the INSERT, so two concurrent creates of the same code can race.
307	- Only BankAccounts.php and Customers.php stop currency changes once transactions exist. SupplierContacts.php, notes and contact pages have no such rule.
308	- Customers.php's `ClientSince` format is checked by `Is_Date` and written through `FormatDateForSQL`; AddCustomerNotes.php writes `NoteDate` through `FormatDateForSQL` without a date check.
309	- A change to a Z_ utility's table list reaches only that utility. Other pages keep their own queries, so adding a new table that references a customer, branch, GL account, salesman or supplier code requires editing each utility.
310	
311	## Hazards
312	- No permission check is shown on any of these pages, including the Z_ utilities that rewrite keys across the database.
313	- SQL is built by concatenating POST and GET values. No escaping is shown in these pages.
314	- A failure in a Z_ transaction that does not use the rollback flag leaves autocommit at 0 and foreign-key checks possibly off, until the request ends.
315	- Z_ChangeGLAccountCode.php deletes the old `chartmaster` row after the commit, so a failure there leaves both rows.
316	- Z_ChangeSalesmanCode.php turns foreign-key checks on again only after the commit.
317	- Customers.php delete leaves `www_users` and `contracts` rows pointing at a deleted customer.
318	- Customers.php `GetNextTransNo(500)` consumes a number even when the INSERT then fails.
319	- There is no check that `DebtorNo` exists in AddCustomerContacts.php, AddCustomerNotes.php or AddCustomerTypeNotes.php.
320	- CustomerBranches.php reads `addrsss1`–`addrsss6` (misspelled) when pre-filling from `debtorsmaster`.
321	- Contact and note deletes have no audit of who deleted what, apart from the generic `audittrail` when `MonthsAuditTrail > 0`.
322	
323	## Open first
324	- `webERP/Customers.php`: customer create, update and delete logic, with its form pages.
325	- `webERP/BankAccounts.php`: bank account maintenance and the currency-lock rule.
326	- `webERP/Z_ChangeGLAccountCode.php`: the largest rename and its table list.
327	- `webERP/Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php`, `webERP/Z_ChangeBranchCode.php`, `webERP/Z_ChangeSalesmanCode.php`, `webERP/Z_ChangeSupplierCode.php`: code renames.
328	- `webERP/AddCustomerContacts.php`, `webERP/AddCustomerNotes.php`, `webERP/AddCustomerTypeNotes.php`, `webERP/SupplierContacts.php`: contact and note maintenance.
329	- `webERP/includes/ConnectDB_mysqli.php`: `DB_query` and the transaction helpers.
330	
331	## Connected topics
332	
333	Topics this one exchanges work or records with, wherever they sit in the map (paths from the export's root):
334	
335	- [SelectCustomer.php: customer search, selection and customer menu (webERP)](weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/selectcustomer-php-customer-search-selection-and-customer-me-87/brief.md)

337	  - it took from this topic's `webERP/AddCustomerTypeNotes.php`: validation rules, insert, update and delete on `debtortypenotes`, and no permission check.
338	  - it took from this topic's `webERP/CustLoginSetup.php`: needs `$_SESSION['CustomerID']` or redirects to `SelectCustomer.php`. Inserts `www_users` with the values listed. No duplicate check on UserID.
339	- [webERP/CustomerBranches.php: customer branch maintenance page (list…](weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/weberp-customerbranches-php-customer-branch-maintenance-page-91/brief.md)
340	  - it took from this topic's `webERP/Customers.php`: redirect and link to `CustomerBranches.php?DebtorNo=` at lines 268 and 272.
341	  - this topic took from `webERP/CustomerBranches.php`: branch validation, geocoding, delete guards, the DebtorNo requirement, and the `addrsss` misspelling.
342	- [webERP includes: database connection, session/login bootstrap, page…](weberp-installer-seed-data-schema-build-ci-and-project-histo-150/weberp-includes-database-connection-session-login-bootstrap--50/brief.md)

# webERP master-data maintenance pages: customer contacts and notes, customers, bank accounts, supplier contacts, and the Z_Change*Code utilities

Part of [webERP: sales, purchasing, stock, manufacturing, master data, reporting, API…](weberp-sales-purchasing-stock-manufacturing-master-data-repo-151/brief.md) (path from the export's root): its brief says how work moves through the area and what repairs a failed step.

These are PHP pages that read and write webERP master-data tables directly through `DB_query`. The main groups are customer contacts and notes, customer-type notes, customer create/update/delete, bank accounts, and supplier contacts. A second group is the Z_ utilities that rename a branch, customer, GL account, salesman or supplier code across the tables that reference it. Customers.php hands the user on to CustomerBranches.php and AddCustomerContacts.php. The pages take work from the user's browser forms. Caller pages are SelectCustomer.php and the others listed under Connections.

## Contract

**Inputs (HTTP GET/POST, no other message type)**
- AddCustomerContacts.php:
  - `Id` (int) and `DebtorNo`, from GET or POST.
  - POST `ContactName` (≤40, required), `ContactRole`, `ContactPhone`, `ContactEmail`, `ContactNotes`, `StatementAddress` (0/1), `Con_ID`, `submit`.
  - GET `delete`.
- AddCustomerNotes.php:
  - `Id` and `DebtorNo`, from GET or POST.
  - POST `NoteDate`, `Priority`, `Note` (≤200), `Href`, `submit`.
  - GET `delete`.
- AddCustomerTypeNotes.php:
  - `Id` (int), `DebtorType` and `NoteDate`.
  - `Priority`, `Note` (≤200), `Href`.
  - `submit` and GET `delete`.
- BankAccounts.php:
  - `SelectedBankAccount`.
  - POST `AccountCode`, `BankAccountName`, `BankAccountCode`, `BankAccountNumber`, `BankAddress`, `CurrCode`, `DefAccount`, `ImportFormat`, `submit`.
  - GET `delete`.
- Customers.php:
  - POST `DebtorNo`, `CustName`, `Address1–6`, `CurrCode`, `ClientSince`, `HoldReason`, `PaymentTerms`, `Discount`, `DiscountCode`, `PymtDiscount`, `CreditLimit`.
  - POST `SalesType`, `AddrInvBranch`, `TaxRef`, `CustomerPOLine`, `typeid`, `LanguageID`, `New`, `submit`, `delete`, `Reset`, `AddContact`.
  - GET `DebtorNo`, `Edit`, `Modify`, `ID`, `Add`.
- SupplierContacts.php:
  - `SupplierID` and `SelectedContact`.
  - POST `Contact`, `Email`, `Position`, `Tel`, `Fax`, `Mobile` (the last three match `[\d\s+()-]{1,30}`), `submit`.
  - GET `delete`.
- Z_ChangeBranchCode.php: `DebtorNo`, `OldBranchCode`, `NewBranchCode`, `ProcessCustomerChange`.
- Z_ChangeCustomerCode.php: `OldDebtorNo`, `NewDebtorNo` (max 20), `ProcessCustomerChange`.
- Z_ChangeGLAccountCode.php: `OldAccountCode`, `NewAccountCode` (upper-cased), `ProcessGLAccountCode`.
- Z_ChangeSalesmanCode.php: `OldSalesmanCode`, `NewSalesmanCode` (4 chars, upper-cased), `ProcessSalesmanChange`.
- Z_ChangeSupplierCode.php: `OldSupplierNo`, `NewSupplierNo` (max 20), `ProcessSupplierChange`.

**Writes**
- All writes go through `DB_query` to these tables:
  - Customer side: `custcontacts`, `custnotes`, `debtortypenotes`, `debtorsmaster`, `custbranch`.
  - Bank and supplier side: `bankaccounts`, `suppliercontacts`.
  - The Z_ utilities write to every table listed in their own entries below.
- Customers.php redirects with a META Refresh to `CustomerBranches.php?DebtorNo=[DebtorNo]` after a successful insert.
- Customers.php redirects to `AddCustomerContacts.php?DebtorNo=` when `AddContact` is non-empty.

## Entry points and guards (in the order they run)

**AddCustomerContacts.php**
1. `if isset($_POST['submit'])` -> validate.
   - `isset(Con_ID) AND !is_long((int)Con_ID)` -> InputError=1, "The Contact ID must be an integer."
   - `mb_strlen(ContactName) > 40` -> InputError=1.
   - `trim(ContactName) == ''` -> InputError=1.
   - `!IsEmailAddress(ContactEmail) AND mb_strlen(ContactEmail) > 0` -> InputError=1.
   - `isset(Id) AND Id AND InputError != 1` -> UPDATE `custcontacts` WHERE contid=Id AND debtorno=DebtorNo.
   - `!isset(Id) AND InputError != 1` -> INSERT `custcontacts` (debtorno, contactname, role, phoneno, notes, email, statement).
   - `InputError != 1` -> unset POST fields and Id.
2. `if isset($_GET['delete']) and $_GET['delete']` -> DELETE `custcontacts` WHERE contid=Id AND debtorno=DebtorNo.
3. `if !isset(Id)` -> list contacts for DebtorNo ORDER BY contid.
   - Rows show `statement` 0 as 'No' and 1 as 'Yes'.
   - The delete link asks "Are you sure you wish to delete this contact?".
4. `if isset(Id)` -> edit form pre-populated.

**AddCustomerNotes.php**
1. `if isset($_POST['submit'])` -> validate.
   - `!is_long((int)Priority)` -> InputError=1.
   - `mb_strlen(Note) > 200` -> InputError=1.
   - `trim(Note) == ''` -> InputError=1.
   - `isset(Id) AND InputError != 1` -> UPDATE `custnotes` (note, date via FormatDateForSQL, href, priority) WHERE debtorno, noteid.
   - `!isset(Id) AND InputError != 1` -> INSERT `custnotes`.
2. `elseif isset($_GET['delete'])` -> DELETE `custnotes` WHERE noteid, debtorno.
3. `if !isset($Id)` -> list ORDER BY date DESC.
4. `if isset($Id)` -> edit form.
5. Defaults: NoteDate=date('Y-m-d') if not set, Priority='1'.

**AddCustomerTypeNotes.php**
1. `if isset($_POST['submit'])` -> the Priority, Note length and Note empty checks are the same as in AddCustomerNotes.php.
   - `isset($Id) and InputError != 1` -> UPDATE `debtortypenotes`.
   - Otherwise, `InputError != 1` -> INSERT `debtortypenotes`.
2. `if isset($_GET['delete'])` -> DELETE `debtortypenotes` WHERE noteid AND typeid.
3. It also reads `typename` from `debtortype` and lists notes ORDER BY date DESC.
4. Default Priority is '1' and default NoteDate is today.

**BankAccounts.php**
1. `if isset($_POST['submit'])` -> validate.
   - `AccountCode` already in `bankaccounts` AND `!isset($SelectedBankAccount)` -> InputError=1.
   - `mb_strlen(BankAccountName) > 50` -> InputError=1.
   - `trim(BankAccountName) == ''` -> InputError=1.
   - `trim(BankAccountNumber) == ''` -> InputError=1.
   - `mb_strlen(BankAccountNumber) > 50` -> InputError=1.
   - `mb_strlen(BankAddress) > 50` -> InputError=1.
   - `isset($SelectedBankAccount) AND InputError != 1` and `banktrans` rows for the account exist -> UPDATE without `currcode`, warning "Note that it is not possible to change the currency of the account once there are transactions against it".
   - The same case with no `banktrans` rows -> UPDATE including `currcode`.
   - `!isset($SelectedBankAccount) AND InputError != 1` -> INSERT.
2. `if isset($_GET['delete'])`:
   - Rows in `banktrans` WHERE bankact -> CancelDelete=1, "Cannot delete this bank account because transactions have been created using this account".
   - `!CancelDelete` -> DELETE `bankaccounts` WHERE accountcode.
3. The form:
   - Edit loads the record, with a hidden AccountCode.
   - Create shows a dropdown of `chartmaster` LEFT JOIN `accountgroups` WHERE `accountgroups.pandl = 0` ORDER BY accountcode.
   - CurrCode and DefAccount default to `$_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['currencydefault']` when missing or ''.
   - `DefAccount` options are 1 "Fall Back Default", 2 "Currency Default" and 0 "No".
   - `ImportFormat` options are '', 'MT940-SCB', 'MT940-ING' and 'GIFTS'.
   - The list shows ImportFormat 'MT940-ING' as 'ING MT940' and 'MT940-SCB' as 'SCB MT940'; any other value shows as ''.

**Customers.php** (`if isset($_POST['submit'])`)
- Validation:
  - `isset(New) AND DebtorNo exists in debtorsmaster` -> InputError=1.
  - `mb_strlen(CustName) > 40 OR == 0` -> InputError=1.
  - `AutoDebtorNo==0 AND mb_strlen(DebtorNo)==0` -> InputError=1.
  - `AutoDebtorNo==0 AND (ContainsIllegalCharacters(DebtorNo) OR mb_strpos(DebtorNo,' '))` -> InputError=1.
  - Address1, 2 and 3 over 40 characters -> InputError=1.
  - Address4 over 50 characters -> InputError=1.
  - Address5 over 20 characters -> InputError=1.
  - CreditLimit, PymtDiscount or Discount `!is_numeric(filter_number_format(..))` -> InputError=1.
  - `!Is_Date(ClientSince)` -> InputError=1.
  - `CreditLimit < 0` -> InputError=1.
  - `PymtDiscount > 10 OR < 0` -> InputError=1.
  - `Discount > 100 OR < 0` -> InputError=1.
- Save:
  - `InputError != 1 AND !isset(New)` and `debtortrans` count == 0 for DebtorNo -> UPDATE `debtorsmaster` with all fields including `currcode`.
  - The same case with `debtortrans` count > 0 -> UPDATE without `currcode`, message "The currency code cannot be updated as there are already transactions for this customer".
  - `InputError != 1 AND isset(New) AND AutoDebtorNo==1` -> `GetNextTransNo(500)` sets DebtorNo.
  - `InputError != 1 AND isset(New)` -> INSERT `debtorsmaster`, with `clientsince` through FormatDateForSQL and Discount and PymtDiscount divided by 100. Then it redirects to `CustomerBranches.php?DebtorNo=`.
  - `InputError == 1` -> no write, "Validation failed. No updates or deletes took place".
- Delete, run when `isset($_POST['delete'])`, in this order:
  - `debtortrans` count > 0 -> CancelDelete=1.
  - `elseif salesorders` count > 0 -> CancelDelete=1.
  - `elseif salesanalysis` (`cust`) count > 0 -> CancelDelete=1.
  - `elseif www_users` (`customerid`) count > 0 -> warning only, CancelDelete NOT set.
  - `elseif contracts` count > 0 -> warning only, CancelDelete NOT set.
  - `CancelDelete==0` -> DELETE `custbranch`, then `custcontacts`, then `debtorsmaster` (all WHERE debtorno). It unsets `$_SESSION['CustomerID']` and exits.
- Form pages:
  - If `COUNT(typeabbrev)` of `salestypes` is 0, or `COUNT(typeid)` of `debtortype` is 0, the page warns and exits (`SetupErrors > 0`).
  - `$_GET['Modify']` makes the fields read-only. `!isset($_POST['New'])` loads the record from `debtorsmaster`.
  - Buttons: `isset(New) AND New` shows "Add New Customer" and Reset; `elseif !isset($_GET['Modify'])` shows "Update Customer" and Delete with a confirm.
  - The form submits only when `$DataError == 0`.
- Contact delete inside the form page: `isset($_GET['delete'])` -> DELETE `custcontacts` WHERE debtorno AND contid, "Contact Deleted".
